Conduct the adaptive continuous wavelet transform on a time series or signal

Source: R/analyse_Awavelet.R, R/zzz_aliases_american.R
analyse_Awavelet.Rd

Compute the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) using a complex Morlet wavelet with scale dependent wavelet width. The number of oscillatory cycles in the Morlet wavelet is allowed to vary smoothly with scale, enabling adaptive time frequency resolution similar in spirit to superlet based approaches.

Usage

analyse_Awavelet(
  data = NULL,
  dj = 1/100,
  lowerPeriod = 2,
  upperPeriod = 1024,
  verbose = FALSE,
  omega_min = 6,
  omega_max = 12,
  scaling = c("none", "log2", "linear", "sqrt", "quadratic", "power"),
  alpha = 1,
  n_simulations = 10,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  wavelet = "morlet",
  wavelet_order = NULL
)

analyze_Awavelet(
  data = NULL,
  dj = 1/100,
  lowerPeriod = 2,
  upperPeriod = 1024,
  verbose = FALSE,
  omega_min = 6,
  omega_max = 12,
  scaling = c("none", "log2", "linear", "sqrt", "quadratic", "power"),
  alpha = 1,
  n_simulations = 10,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  wavelet = "morlet",
  wavelet_order = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Input record: a matrix or data frame with depth/time in column 1 and the proxy value in column 2. Rows with NA are removed, the rows are sorted by depth/time and the record is linearly interpolated to an even spacing equal to the median sampling interval. Required (Default=NULL gives an error).

dj

Spacing between successive scales in octaves (numeric, > 0): scales increase as 2^(j * dj), so 1/100 gives 100 scales per doubling of the period. Smaller values give a finer period axis at the cost of computation time. Default=1/100.

lowerPeriod

Shortest period to analyse, in the same unit as the depth/time column of data (numeric, > 0; at least twice the sampling interval). Default=2.

upperPeriod

Longest period to analyse, in the same unit as the depth/time column of data (numeric, > lowerPeriod; normally not more than the length of the record). Default=1024.

verbose

Print the sampling interval to which the record was interpolated (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

omega_min

Number of oscillatory cycles of the Morlet wavelet (omega_0) at the shortest period (numeric, > 0, typically 5 to 6). Fewer cycles give a better depth/time resolution, more cycles a better period resolution. Default=6.

omega_max

Number of oscillatory cycles of the Morlet wavelet at the longest period (numeric, > 0). The number of cycles changes from omega_min to omega_max along the period axis as set by scaling. Default=12.

scaling

How the number of wavelet cycles changes from omega_min (shortest period) to omega_max (longest period) (character), one of:

  • "none": linear in the scale index, which is equivalent to linear in log2(period);

  • "log2": linear in log2(period);

  • "linear": linear in period;

  • "sqrt": with the square root of the normalised log2(period) (fast change at short periods);

  • "quadratic": with the square of the normalised log2(period) (fast change at long periods);

  • "power": with the normalised log2(period) to the power alpha.

Default="none" (the first element of c("none", "log2", "linear", "sqrt", "quadratic", "power")).

alpha

Exponent of the "power" scaling (numeric, > 0); only used when scaling="power". Values greater than 1 keep the number of cycles close to omega_min over most of the period range and increase it mainly at the longest periods; values smaller than 1 do the opposite. Default=1.

n_simulations

Number of Monte Carlo simulations (integer). Not used: kept only for compatibility with the interface of the other wavelet functions (no significance test is made). Default=10.

run_multicore

Run in parallel on several cores (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Not used: kept only for compatibility with the interface of the other wavelet functions. Default=FALSE.

wavelet

Mother wavelet (character string or function), given as a name (PyWavelets style names with the order appended, such as "db4", "sym8", "cgau3", "gaus2" or "cmor1.5-1", also work) or as a function psi_hat(omega) that returns the Fourier transform of a user defined mother wavelet. Analytic (complex) wavelets, which give phase and amplitude and can be synchrosqueezed: "morlet" (default; aliases "gabor", "amor"), "morlet0" (exactly zero mean Morlet, admissible for a small omega_nr; alias "morlex"), "paul" (alias "cauchy"), "morse" (generalised Morse wavelet of Olhede and Walden, 2002; aliases "gmw", "airy"), "bump", "cmor" (complex Morlet with bandwidth and centre frequency as in Matlab/PyWavelets), "cgau" (analytic Gaussian derivative; "cmhat" is the complex Mexican hat), "shannon" (complex Shannon, box spectrum), "fbsp" (frequency B-spline), "meyer", "loggabor" (alias "lognormal"), "gammatone" (asymmetric in time: sharp onset, slow decay) and "hann" (raised cosine band). Real wavelets, which give a real transform (no phase or envelope): "dog" (derivative of Gaussian; "mexh", "ricker", "marr" and "sombrero" are the Mexican hat, order 2), "morl" (real Morlet), "hhat" (Hermitian hat), "poisson", and the orthogonal wavelets "haar", "db" (Daubechies), "sym" (Symlets) and "battle" (Battle-Lemarie spline wavelets), which are computed in the frequency domain from their filters. The period axis of the orthogonal wavelets is approximate because their spectra are broad and not symmetric. A narrow wavelet (Paul, low-order DOG, Shannon, Haar) resolves position well, a wide one (Morse with a large beta, Morlet with a high number of cycles, bump) resolves period well. For wavelets other than the Morlet, the wavelet at each scale is given the relative bandwidth of a Morlet wavelet with the local number of cycles (between omega_min and omega_max). Default="morlet".

wavelet_order

Parameter(s) of the wavelet (numeric scalar or vector, see analyse_wavelet); when it is NULL the wavelet whose relative bandwidth equals that of a Morlet wavelet with omega_min to omega_max cycles is used at every scale. Parameters of the wavelet: paul: order m (default 4); dog: derivative m (default 2); morse: c(gamma, beta) or beta alone with gamma = 3 (default c(3, 20)); bump: c(mu, sigma) (default c(5, 0.6)); cmor: c(bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(1.5, 1)); cgau: derivative m (default 4); shannon: c(bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(2, 1.5)); fbsp: c(m, bandwidth, centre frequency) (default c(2, 2, 1.5)); loggabor: c(centre angular frequency, log-width) (default c(6, 0.25)); meyer and hhat have no parameter; morlet0: omega_0 (default: the local number of cycles); morl: omega_0 (default 5); poisson: order n (default 2); gammatone: c(n, centre angular frequency, bandwidth) (default c(4, 6, 1.5)); hann: c(centre angular frequency, half width) (default c(6, 3)); db: number of vanishing moments 1 to 20 (default 4, "haar" = "db1"); sym: 2 to 20 (default 8); battle: spline order 1, 3, 5 or 7 (default 3). For the Morlet wavelet use omega_min and omega_max; a non-NULL wavelet_order uses one fixed wavelet at all scales. Default=NULL.

Value

A list with class "analyze.Awavelet" containing:

  • Wave: complex wavelet coefficients

  • Phase: instantaneous phase

  • Ampl: wavelet amplitude

  • Power: wavelet power spectrum

  • dt: sampling interval

  • dj: scale spacing

  • Power.avg: average power per period

  • Period: physical periods

  • Scale: wavelet scales

  • coi.1: cone of influence x coordinates

  • coi.2: cone of influence y coordinates

  • nc: number of samples

  • nr: number of scales

  • axis.1: x axis values

  • axis.2: log2 scaled periods

  • omega_min: minimum wavelet cycles

  • omega_max: maximum wavelet cycles

  • omega: scale dependent wavelet cycles

  • scaling: scaling method used

  • alpha: power law exponent

  • x: interpolated x values

  • y: interpolated signal values

References

Torrence, C., and G. P. Compo (1998). A practical guide to wavelet analysis. Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society, 79, 61–78.

Morlet, J., G. Arens, E. Fourgeau, and D. Giard (1982). Wave propagation and sampling theory. Geophysics, 47, 203–236.

Author

Adapted from the WaveletComp and biwavelet R packages, which are based on the MATLAB wavelet code by Torrence and Compo, with extensions for scale dependent wavelet width.

Examples

# \donttest{
#Example 1. Using the Total Solar Irradiance data set of Steinhilber et al., (2012)
TSI_wt <-
 analyse_Awavelet(
   data = TSI,
   dj = 1/200,
   lowerPeriod = 16,
   upperPeriod = 8192,
   verbose = FALSE,
omega_min = 6,
omega_max = 12,
scaling = "log2",
alpha = 1
 )


#Example 2. Using the magnetic susceptibility data set of Pas et al., (2018)
mag_wt <-
analyse_Awavelet(
data = mag,
dj = 1/100,
lowerPeriod = 0.1,
upperPeriod = 254,
verbose = FALSE,
omega_min = 6,
omega_max = 12,
scaling = "log2",
alpha = 1
)

#Example 3. Using the greyscale data set of Zeeden et al., (2013)
grey_wt <-
 analyse_Awavelet(
   data = grey,
   dj = 1/200,
   lowerPeriod = 0.02,
   upperPeriod = 256,
   verbose = FALSE,
omega_min = 6,
omega_max = 12,
scaling = "log2",
alpha = 1,
 )

# }
